output.name: Nasmi
output.myth: When Aun cut the string, Mother Hesk counted every dead thing that went up with the sky, and her count was right. What she could not count was the rope. Nasmi is old rope undone past where the wind turns back, each strand gone its own road into the tar-smelling dark. Ennu once tried to lay them up again, the way a sail is laid, but his hands cramped and he let them go. Halesk, the Stilled Gull, hangs above that dark with her neck stretched out like a hand asking for rain, too proud to come down. Two fists west, Skelmi still waits on her last feather for a woman who died before it was sewn. Tikar, the small boot the sea kept, burns in the north-west, and Tirka's cliff-ladder hangs out to the east with no one on it. So the strands sing alone, thin and cold, toward knots that were never theirs. That is why the old women say: do not untwist what you are sad to lose. Keep your knots tied. Keep counting.
output.finding: Nasmi never rises over the islands, so sailors far south find it by going to the Stilled Gull, the brightest star of the Unflown, and looking a hand-span and a little more south-west of her for the faint strands.
